title: Write Your First JavaScript Step
description: Drop into JavaScript when the declarative configuration runs out.
openingSummary: Declarative configuration covers most flow logic. When it does not, a JavaScript step lets you compute the next move in code without leaving the factory.

whatItIs.title: What It Is
whatItIs.body: A JavaScript step is an ordinary function the runtime calls with the current work state. It returns the next state, and the graph carries on from there.

whenToUse.title: When To Use
whenToUse.body: Use JavaScript when a decision depends on something the declarative form cannot express: parsing a payload, calling out to your own service, or branching on a computed value.

stepsOrWorkflow.title: Steps Or Workflow
stepsOrWorkflow.body: Add a script worker to your factory, write the function, then run the factory and read the step's output in the logs.

commonPitfalls.title: Common Pitfalls
commonPitfalls.body: Keep the step small and pure where you can. A JavaScript step that does its own retries, its own logging, and its own error handling is competing with the runtime rather than using it.
